$comment: ROADMAP Phase 1A step 3 - camera behaviour. Engine-neutral canon (Rule 22 / Decision 0002). CPU vs. CPU is a first-class spectator experience (Rule 7), so the camera is a readability instrument before it is a spectacle instrument. Definitions only - no engine implementation is claimed (Rule 18). Every number is a tuning hypothesis. Semantics: docs/phase1a/camera_behavior.md.

authority.$comment: The camera is downstream of truth and cannot bend it.

framing_modes.description: A stoppage or doctor decision is resolving. The camera holds the decisive subject and does not cut away for spectacle.
framing_modes.notes: Rule 8's clarity-over-queued-dialogue principle applied to framing: event clarity outranks presentation flourish.

framing_modes.description: A fighter is down or rising. Frames the downed fighter, the count, and the neutral-corner instruction together so the count is legible.
framing_modes.notes: The referee's count is the authority; the camera must never imply a different count state.

framing_modes.description: Clock is in the count segment: wide enough to hold downed fighter, referee and neutral corner.
Medical inspection. Frames the inspected region and the official; side-specific eye damage must be visibly attributable (Rule 14).
Clinch or inside work. Tightens without losing either fighter's hands, so legal inside work stays distinguishable from fouling (Rule 16).
Comedy and Showmanship beat: a brief punch-in on an authored flourish. Comedy is the highest PRESENTATION priority (Rule 17), and it still yields to every officiating and safety mode above.
framing_modes.notes: Hard tick cap: the joke never outlasts the boxing. Rule 19 orders responsiveness and readability above humour in game feel even though comedy leads presentation.

framing_modes.description: Live exchange at boxing range. The default working shot: both fighters, both guards, and the space between them, so a spectator can attribute cause to effect (criterion F.24).
Fighters out of range: ring position, ropes and corners readable, so Ringcraft is visible rather than inferred.
Between-round break: corner work and condition are visible. The break clock is not paused by presentation (Rule 9).
Entrances and referee disclosure (Rule 16). Character presentation lives here, where it costs no combat readability.
Result and immediate post-fight flow. Official cards stay sealed through this segment (Rule 3) - the camera has no privileged view of them.
Fallback working shot when no other mode claims the tick. Guarantees the selector is total.

readability.$comment: Rule 19: visual speed may not destroy readable cause and effect. These are the structural guards.

prohibitions: Read official scorecards or any sealed event - the camera is named in Rule 3's live-replay-presentation list.
Write, nudge or gate any simulation state, including fighter position, timing, stamina or contact classification.
Frame so that a whiffed or blocked punch reads as a clean landed punch (Rule 13's presentation half).
Cut between a punch's active window and its outcome event.
Hold a showmanship or comedy flourish through a knockdown, count, doctor check or stoppage.
Depend on wall-clock time, frame rate or render timing for any decision; all timing is tick-anchored.
Hide accumulated condition that the simulation considers decisive - eye and guard damage must remain visually attributable (Rule 14).

invariants.statement: The camera writes no simulation state; resimulation is independent of presentation.
Camera inputs are observable-only; official cards and sealed events are unreachable from framing decisions.
Priorities form a strict total order and a default mode exists, so exactly one framing mode is selected every tick - camera behaviour is inspectable and never ambiguous.
Stoppage, knockdown, count and doctor modes outrank every spectacle mode; comedy leads presentation but never obscures officiating.
Every mode that can be active during the round segment keeps both fighters framed, and no cut may fall inside a contact window.
Camera distance bands are exactly the movement model's range bands; framing follows position rather than redefining it.
Every camera duration is expressed in ticks; wall-clock and frame-rate dependence do not exist in the model.
Framing is a pure function of the observable event log and tick, so replay reproduces recorded presentation without rerunning uncertain decisions.
